Prediction markets give people something they need to make better decisions: reliable probabilities that update as new information comes in.

Kalshi looked at more than 2.2 million observations. When the market gave an outcome a 30% chance with a month to go, outcomes priced at those odds happened about 30% of the time.

That’s especially useful in election analysis. Polls show what voters want, while prediction markets show how available information and incoming results change the odds of a candidate winning or a party taking control of Congress.

The same kind of information helps investors decide how much risk to hedge before a Fed meeting, farmers prepare for extreme weather, and small businesses decide whether to stock up ahead of a potential tariff hike.

🚨BREAKING: Tim Burchett is torching Senate Leader John Thune for sitting on legislation meant to stop U.S. taxpayer money from reaching the Taliban.

Burchett’s “No Tax Dollars for Terrorists Act” passed the House and would require the State Department to develop a strategy to stop foreign countries and NGOs from providing financial or material support to the Taliban. He has repeatedly pointed to reports of roughly $40 million a week in U.S.-linked cash and aid flowing into Afghanistan since the 2021 withdrawal, with total assistance exceeding $5 billion. Watchdog reports have documented the Taliban skimming taxes, fees, and other payments from that aid.

The bill has languished in the Senate. Burchett says he personally raised it with Thune and was told it is not a priority. He has publicly questioned why the Senate will not simply take it up if the money is not reaching the Taliban.

The House already acted. The Senate under Thune has not. Taxpayers deserve an explanation for why legislation aimed at cutting off funds to the group that now controls Afghanistan keeps getting ignored.
